eligibility.exact_action_basis: The whole House text requires Energy and Agriculture to carry out cross-cutting collaborative research and development addressing their joint mission requirements and priorities, coordinated through a memorandum of understanding or other appropriate interagency agreement. That agreement must require a competitive, merit-reviewed process considering Federal agencies, National Laboratories, higher education, nonprofits and other appropriate applicants. The enumerated coordination activities are optional: listed scientific/engineering and agriculture–energy research areas; voluntary standardized/integrated datasets; secure, legally compliant information sharing; research infrastructure/workforce support as necessary; and research/development/demonstration methods to improve agricultural efficiency and reduce related emissions. The list includes AI/modeling/data methods, fuels including aviation/naval applications, energy/agriculture and carbon-technology colocation, invasive-species work, long-term/high-risk technology, grid modernization/security, rural technologies and wildfire/energy-infrastructure research. It does not require every focus, dataset, partner or demonstration. Reimbursable agreements and other-agency collaboration are authorized; a report to the four named congressional committees is due within two years after enactment. Activities must be applied consistently with the named2022 research-security subtitle. That retained subtitle distinguishes agency-personnel foreign-talent restrictions from covered-individual malign-program restrictions, with certification/training, international-collaboration exceptions, privacy/evidentiary/rebuttal protections and nondiscrimination requirements. The bill does not create a universal ban on international research. Its optional ARPA-E collaboration reference does not amend ARPA-E, appropriate its dated authorized amounts or automatically impose every ARPA-E project predicate on all joint work. The bill itself supplies no new appropriation or proof of an implemented research program.

Perry amendment25 to H.R.4553 would append a $350million reduction at RHpage33line12 and a $350million increase at page74line5. The first target is the entire $350million ARPA-E appropriation for section5012 activities, not only overhead; the second is section512’s initially zero Spending Reduction Account. The target also retains a $40million OF THAT AMOUNT program-direction proviso available through September30,2027, which the amendment does not delete. The literal reduced topline is zero while that nested proviso remains printed. This candidate preserves that interaction and does not decide that $40million remains independently available, that a negative appropriation arises, or how the unchanged proviso would legally operate. The retained ARPA-E law describes long-term/high-risk transformative energy technology research and several award/transfer mechanisms; its dated authorizations are not the bill appropriation or actual spending. The amendment neither repeals ARPA-E nor expressly rescinds all previously available program funding. The House rejected this exact amendment77–347, after preliminary voice ayes and postponement; the recorded rejection controls. Opposition or support concerns these two textual instructions as a whole, not every ARPA-E project, the agency’s existence or parent-bill passage.

Perry amendment27 would append a $35million reduction to RHpage33line24’s general-fund administrative appropriation for the Title17 Innovative Technology Loan Guarantee Program and add $35million to the initially zero Spending Reduction Account. The heading separately permits up to $35million of FY2026 fees for administration through September30,2027; excess collections need future advance appropriations. Its general-fund line is reduced as current fees and qualified prior fees are received, with a final general-fund appropriation already estimated at zero. The amendment does not delete those fee-credit/use/offset provisos. The legal availability and interaction of those unchanged clauses after reducing the line remain unresolved; neither elimination of all administrative resources nor a $35million net Treasury saving follows automatically. The distinct $150million appropriation for COSTS of eligible small-modular/advanced-nuclear loan guarantees remains, with non-subordination, non-federal source-of-payment, defined federal-support restrictions/exceptions and advance written OMB certification. It is not $150million of loan principal. Dated Title17 law distinguishes subsidy/guarantee costs, conditional project eligibility, repayment, fees and audit duties; the ordinary lesser-of30years/90percent-life term is distinct from the printed1706 override. The later July2025 law rescinds specified unobligated balances, changes1706 energy-infrastructure eligibility, removes specified former requirements and adds $1billion through September30,2028 with no more than3percent for administration. This amendment does not repeal or establish exhaustion of that separate authority/funding. The House rejected amendment27 by120–306; neither its proposed line edit nor its fiscal consequences were enacted by that vote.

Roy amendment32, offered by Perry as designee, would reduce RHpage26line13’s $1.83billion EERE appropriation by $1.83billion and its page26line14 $223million program-direction amount by $223million. The direction amount is expressly OF THE SAME SUM; the two resulting printed amounts are zero, not a $2.053billion additive cut. There is no Spending Reduction Account instruction. The whole account funds energy-efficiency/renewable-energy activities, including specified plant, capital-equipment and property/facility purposes; direction has a September30,2027 availability limit while the main amount remains until expended. Section301 incorporates the accompanying report’s Bill-column allocations, with defined notice, multiyear-funding, reprogramming restrictions and substantial-risk waiver/notice, and permits qualified prior balances to remain/merge on their originally enacted availability period. The retained report’s selected EERE narrative/table evidence covers transportation, renewable energy, efficiency, State/community energy, manufacturing and facilities/support. Its selected table subtotals—including the nested $223million direction and $195million weatherization allocation—are components of $1.83billion, not extra appropriations or a medical-only account. This is a proposed removal of this bill’s new whole-account funding; it does not repeal statutory authorities, expressly rescind all prior balances, establish an agency shutdown or identify which household/project would lose services. The House rejected this exact amendment127–297; no enacted funding loss or actual technological, health or environmental outcome follows. Both members’ observations concern this same whole instruction, not separate preferences on each EERE program.

The whole House text would require FERC to initiate a rulemaking within90days of enactment and finalize regulations within180days to amend the pro forma Large Generator Interconnection Procedures and, as appropriate, Agreement under the printed18CFR35.28(f) reference. It would authorize defined transmission providers to propose higher queue positions for new dispatchable projects that improve grid reliability AND resource adequacy. Each proposal must demonstrate need and describe improvement to grid reliability OR grid resilience, after a public-comment/stakeholder process before submission. FERC must review and approve or deny within60days after submission; providers must report regularly on reliability/resilience and actions under the Act. At least every five years FERC reviews the regulations and updates them if necessary. Dispatchable power is defined by known/forecastable supply over reliability-relevant time intervals, without an enumerated fuel list; this is not a finding that a named fuel/project automatically qualifies. The incorporated bulk-power definition excludes local-distribution facilities, and the retained RTO/ISO/public-utility definitions keep their jurisdiction/approval qualifications; no general federal jurisdiction expansion is inferred. H.Res.707section4 deems RCP119-9 adopted; the complete RCP and own printed floor operative body conform to the retained EH, and the separate recorded roll279 passes it216–206. This is passage of the whole rulemaking/proposal framework, not an automatic queue jump, guarantee of project approval/construction, or proof that processing, price or reliability improved.
